    You are the construction manager

    Build a data center campus, one phase at a time

    For ages 12 and up · about 20 minutes · no sign-up, no personal data.

    A project by A2 Learning Studio

    Class mode: the game never starts over by itself, and this tab keeps it until the tab is closed.

    Home mode: the game never starts over by itself, and this tab keeps it until the tab is closed.

    Red Clay Ridge is a made-up site of about 45 acres off a county road in Georgia, next to a street of homes. A company wants a data center campus there. Your job is to build it in the right order, keep the schedule, the budget and the crew safe, and work with the neighbors. The game shows facts and trade-offs. It does not take a side on data centers.

    Pick a phase, place each of its key elements, then finish the phase. Issue cards will interrupt you. Your choices move the dashboard and the neighborhood panel.

    Keys: Tab moves between buttons · Enter or Space presses · N = next step · M = effects on the map on/off · V = voice on/off (these three can be turned off in About) · on the map, arrow keys turn, + or − zoom, and Shift + arrow keys move when zoomed in. While you are siting a piece, drag or tap the map: letting go on a spot that fits builds it there. Or nudge it with the arrow keys, then press N or Set it here. The game asks you to decide when each choice matters.

    Using a screen reader? Turn the recorded voice off for this game, so it does not talk over your reader.

          Build the Campus

          A project by A2 Learning Studio

          The site, company and neighbors are made up. The rules and the facts in the Neighbors panel are real as of October 2026 (sources below); costs, delays and points are simplified game values, not estimates for a real project. Durations are typical ranges and vary by project. In real life a county can approve, change or deny a rezoning; in this game it approves the plan, so you can see what building it takes. The emissions from making the extra electricity depend on how it is generated.

          A companion to Community Builders of Pecan Grove.

          Ages 12 and up (grade 7 to adult); younger players with an adult. Asks no names and stores nothing about you.

          Privacy: this game collects no personal information. No sign-up, ads, analytics or cookies. Nothing you do is sent anywhere. In class or home mode, this browser may remember the Library mode, presenter view, shortcut and voice settings, and it keeps your game in progress, with a timed list of its steps, until the tab is closed. In those modes the end screen can save that game's choices, scores and steps to this device as a file (JSON, or one spreadsheet row as CSV) with no name in it, and Open results file on the first screen reads one back here without sending it anywhere; a library kiosk offers neither. The host logs IP addresses for security, and your browser keeps an offline copy. In class and home modes, the source links below open other websites.

          Questions, privacy concerns or corrections: akeyvanf@kennesaw.eduakeyvanf@kennesaw.edu

          Map, keys and modes

          Map: drag to turn; scroll, pinch or press + and − to zoom toward the pointer. Zoomed in, a drag (or Shift + arrow keys) moves the view, and right-drag, Shift-drag or two fingers turn it. The buttons on the map do the same, and Reset view brings the whole site back. To site a piece, drag or tap the map (right-drag or two fingers still turn the view). Green fits the setback, the site and the utility rules; a striped red footprint does not, and the Build panel says why. Letting go where the footprint is green builds the piece there. Set it here builds it where the footprint is shown: the suggested spot, or where the arrow keys nudged it.

          Modes: with no mode the game is set up for a library kiosk. It starts over after a few minutes without input and saves nothing, so what a player switches lasts one game. Add ?mode=class or ?mode=home to the address to stop it clearing itself and to keep the game in progress if the page reloads, until the tab is closed. ?mode=library starts each game with the voice off; add &voice=off to ?mode=class or ?mode=home for the same.

          Class mode: the game never starts over by itself, and this tab keeps it until the tab is closed.

          Home mode: the game never starts over by itself, and this tab keeps it until the tab is closed.

          How this is scored. Neighbor relations starts at 35 when grading begins. Choices and issue cards add or remove points. The truck traffic, noise and dust & night lighting rows remove points as they rise; after opening, noise always counts at its lowest level, so the cooling type is not scored. The other rows are information only, because they are not the same kind of effect. Safety starts at 82 and moves with your choices and the issue cards. For safety and neighbor relations, 80 or more is Strong, 60 to 79 Good, 45 to 59 Fair, 30 to 44 Watch and under 30 Concern. The schedule is judged against a 45-month plan: Strong at or under 45 months, Good up to two months over, Fair up to four over, Watch beyond that. The budget adds up what your choices and the issue cards cost, plus 0.3% for every month they add to the finish, because crews, equipment and loans keep costing while the work runs late. The plan holds 3% for surprises: Strong at or under 103% of plan, Good up to 104.5%, Fair up to 106%, Watch beyond that. Cooling changes power use and water use on the panel; it is not a point for or against the project.

          This is the offline kiosk copy: one file with the narration inside. Open it in a full-screen or kiosk browser; it needs no network. Add ?mode=library to the file's address to keep the voice off for every player.

          Browsers and computers

          Needs a current browser: Chrome or Edge 108 or later, Firefox 101 or later, or Safari 15.4 or later (Mac, iPad and iPhone). The 3D map needs WebGL 2 graphics, which most computers, Chromebooks and tablets in use today have. A screen 1280 × 720 or larger works best; phones show a smaller map. Without 3D graphics the panels, the schedule and every choice still work. Accessibility: the game aims to meet WCAG 2.2 level AA. Known limits: the 3D map is visual only, though everything that counts is also in the panels, the schedule and the Site log as text; and the game is in English only. To report a barrier, write to akeyvanf@kennesaw.edu.

          The game picks less 3D detail on slower graphics. Add ?quality=low to the address if the map is slow, or ?quality=high to always use full detail.

          Words to know

          Data center
          a building full of computers called servers that run websites, apps and AI. They use a lot of electricity and give off heat.
          CM (construction manager)
          the person or firm that plans and runs the building work for the owner. In this game, that is you. On real projects the owner and its engineers lead the rezoning and the power agreement, and the construction manager joins early to plan the schedule, estimate the cost and help order long-lead equipment.
          Rezoning
          a county decision, made after a public hearing, that changes what a piece of land may be used for. A county can approve it, approve it with conditions or deny it.
          Critical path
          the chain of steps that sets the finish date. If a step on it slips, the finish slips.
          Long-lead equipment
          equipment built to order, such as large transformers, switchgear and large generators, that takes months or years to arrive, so it is ordered during design.
          Substation and transformer
          equipment that steps high-voltage power down for the campus.
          Heavy haul and escort
          moving an oversized load, such as a large transformer, on a special truck and trailer, with road permits and escort vehicles.
          Switchgear
          large electrical equipment that routes and protects the power inside the building.
          Power skid
          electrical equipment mounted and wired on a steel frame in a factory, then set in place on site.
          MEP (mechanical, electrical & plumbing)
          the systems that power, cool and protect the building.
          UPS (uninterruptible power supply)
          backup batteries that keep the servers running for the seconds before the generators start.
          Closed loop (cooling)
          cooling whose water or coolant stays sealed in pipes and is cooled by air, so it uses little water on site.
          Silt fence and sediment basin
          a fabric fence and ponds that keep muddy water on the site during earthwork.
          Check dam
          a small barrier, often of rock, across a ditch that slows rainwater so the mud settles out.
          Haul road
          a temporary road on the site for trucks and earthmovers.
          Buffer, setback and berm
          the space between the campus and the homes (the setback is the minimum the county allows), and an earth mound that screens them.
          Tilt-up panels
          concrete walls cast flat on the slab and tilted up into place.
          Rigging and safety stand-down
          rigging is the slings, shackles and hooks that hold a load to a crane; a safety stand-down is a pause in the work so the crew can check a hazard together before going on.
          Dried in
          the roof and walls are closed, so rain stays out.
          Commissioning (Levels 1 to 5)
          testing in steps: factory tests, delivery checks, start-up, functional tests, and an integrated test with a planned power cut.
          Load bank
          a machine that draws power and makes heat the way servers do, for testing.
          Punch list
          the last small fixes before handover.
          Turnover
          handing the finished campus to its owner.
          Megawatt (MW)
          a unit of electric power. 100 megawatts running all year uses about as much electricity as 84,000 U.S. homes.
          Contingency
          money held in the budget for surprises.

          The one-page educator sheet, with a kiosk set-up checklist, is on the game's web site: https://a2-learning-studio.github.io/data-center-build-playtest/educator.html

          Durations are typical ranges, simplified for the game; they vary by project. Real projects overlap their phases; the game runs them one after another, except that utilities run alongside grading and building. The five commissioning levels are common industry practice, not a law or standard.
